title: Rigveda 5.71: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.71: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.71 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 388r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.71.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 388r
translation.original_text:
1ā no̍ gantaṁ riśādasā̱ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̍ ba̱rhaṇā̍ | upe̱maṁ cāru̍m adhva̱ram ||
2viśva̍sya̱ hi pra̍cetasā̱ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̱ rāja̍thaḥ | ī̱śā̱nā pi̍pyata̱ṁ dhiya̍ḥ ||
3upa̍ naḥ su̱tam ā ga̍ta̱ṁ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̍ dā̱śuṣa̍ḥ | a̱sya soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
translation.text:
1O Varuṇa and Mitra, ye who slay the foemen, come with might To this our goodly sacrifice.
2For, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye Sages are Rulers over all. Fill full our songs, for this ye can.
3Come to the juice that we have pressed. Varuṇa, Mitra, come to drink This Soma of the worshipper.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 388r (numbered 61r by the scribe) (OPenn image 388, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.70.3 ‹tanū-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 388v (numbered 61v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.73.1 ‹yat adya sthaḥ pārāvati›. Verses 5.71.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1ā | naḥ | gantam | riśādasā | varuṇa | mitra | barhaṇā | upa | imam | cārum | adhvaram
2viśvasya | hi | pra-cetasā | varuṇa | mitra | rājathaḥ | īśānā | pipyatam | dhiyaḥ
3upa | naḥ | sutam | ā | gatam | varuṇa | mitra | dāśuṣaḥ | asya | somasya | pītaye
